overview.what_it_does: Dixon Technologies is an Indian contract manufacturer of electronics and appliances — it does not sell under its own brand, but builds products for other companies' brands out of its factories in India (Noida, Dehradun, Tirupati, Chennai and other locations). Its customers are global and Indian brand owners such as Motorola, Xiaomi, Oppo, Nokia, Jio, the Transsion brands (Tecno, Infinix, Itel), HMD, Acer, Lenovo, HP, Asus, Voltas, Kelvinator, Lloyd, Haier, IKEA and Eureka Forbes, plus telecom operators' equipment suppliers. It earns money on the manufacturing spread — either pure EMS (assembling to the customer's design, thin margins on very large volumes) or ODM, where Dixon designs the product itself and earns more; management repeatedly stresses "backward integration" (making sub-parts such as camera modules, display modules, moulded plastics, LED components and SSDs in-house) as the way to capture more value per unit. Scale is large and fast-growing but low-margin: FY26 revenue of about ₹48,893 crores with EBITDA of ₹1,887 crores and profit after minority interest of ₹845 crores, run with negative working capital and ROCE around 45%.

parts.name: Mobile phones and EMS division
parts.what: Assembles smartphones and feature phones for global and Indian brands, largely on a contract-manufacturing basis, and is by far the biggest part of the company — about ₹9,485 crores of roughly ₹10,520 crores of Q4 FY26 revenue, up from ₹1,410 crores a quarter back in early 2023; it includes JVs with Longcheer and Vivo and the acquired subsidiary Ismartu (export-focused, mainly Africa).

parts.name: Consumer electronics (LED TVs and refrigerators)
parts.what: Makes LED TVs — including premium mini-LED, large-screen and smart models across Google TV, Linux, Tizen, WebOS and Amazon Fire platforms — plus digital signage, interactive flat panel displays and direct-cool refrigerators for brands like Voltas, Kelvinator, Lloyd, BPL and Haier; it was the original core business (₹981 crores in Q4 FY23) but is now a much smaller slice, ₹567 crores in Q3 FY26 at about 4% operating margin.

parts.name: Home appliances
parts.what: Designs and builds washing machines (semi-automatic, fully automatic and now front-loading) and related appliances such as robotic vacuum cleaners for Eureka Forbes, on a full ODM basis; a modest but consistently profitable line at roughly ₹329–₹444 crores a quarter with the best margins in the group, around 11–12%.

parts.name: Lighting
parts.what: Manufactures LED bulbs, downlighters, outdoor and professional lighting and lighting components for Indian and export customers including IKEA and buyers in the UAE and Germany; a small segment, roughly ₹233–₹270 crores a quarter, with high-single-digit operating margins.

parts.name: Telecom and networking products
parts.what: Builds routers, 5G fixed-wireless-access units, access points, GPON/ONT devices, set-top boxes and complex backhaul microwave radios for telecom customers; grew from ₹311 crores for all of FY23 to ₹660 crores in a single quarter by FY25, and management expects high double-digit growth again in FY27 as it shifts from pure assembly to joint design work.

parts.name: IT hardware products (laptops, tablets, desktops)
parts.what: Assembles laptops, tablets, all-in-ones and now desktops at a dedicated Chennai plant and a 60:40 JV with Taiwan's Inventec, with Acer, Lenovo, HP and Asus signed up — four of India's top five brands; management guides to roughly 3x revenue growth in FY27 and is exploring a JV to enter server and data-centre hardware.

parts.name: Components / backward integration (camera modules, display modules, others)
parts.what: A newer push to make the parts that go into its own products — camera and fingerprint modules through subsidiary Q Tech (scaling from about 70 million to 180–190 million units a year), display modules via a 74:26 JV with HKC (24 million units in phase one, rising to 55 million), plus SSDs, enclosures and optical transceivers — mostly captive today, with government ECMS support, and framed by management as the route to higher margins.

parts.name: Wearables and hearables
parts.what: Contract manufacturing of smartwatches and wireless earbuds; a small line at about ₹263 crores a quarter in FY25, but described as having healthy margins and strong returns on capital.

parts.name: Security surveillance systems
parts.what: A 50:50 joint venture making CCTV and surveillance equipment, with capacity expanded from 10 million to 14 million units a year at a Kopparthi plant; Dixon's half-share of revenue was ₹124 crores in Q4 FY23 at thin margins, and Dixon separately held a 6.5% stake in Aditya Infotech that produced a ₹210 crore fair-value gain in FY25.

parts.name: Rexxam Dixon Electronics (JV)
parts.what: A joint venture with Rexxam making electronic control boards, supplying air-conditioner maker Daikin as its main customer; small, at about ₹90 crores of revenue in a seasonally weak quarter.
